root_causes.title: Contaminated-stem dead-end: GOOD question-shaped stems destroyed by the token-containment guard, then retry/rescue loop forever returning the same blocked text
evidence: [SWEEP] q3/q4/q10: stripped contaminated stem (stem text substantially contained in this record's own solution)
[RETRY] blocked contaminated stem for q3/q4/q10 ... still stem-missing (round 1 AND round 2)
[RESCUE] page 14: q4 -> 0 field(s) filled; page 16: q10 -> 0 field(s) filled
SAME pattern in ch2 q25, ch6 q5, ch7 q1/q23-26, ch10 q5, ch11 q1/q17, ch13 q2/q11, ch16 q2/q10
carry-forward used only 1 time in the WHOLE run
root_causes.mechanism: Two compounding bugs: (1) _stem_reject_reason flagged ANY text whose tokens are >=80% contained in the record's own solution -- but medical solutions RESTATE the stem ('The correct answer is B. The patient presents with...'), so short QUESTION-SHAPED stems legitimately passed the threshold and were stripped as 'contaminated' (false positive). (2) When a real contamination re-read arrived, the stem-conflict coherence resolver preferred it (solution-prose coheres perfectly with the solution payload), replacing the GOOD stem -- and the generic merge loop overwrote stems with contaminated text. Result: stem lost -> retry re-asks the same solution pages -> guard blocks the same text every round -> rescue 0 fields -> export-gate missing_stem.
root_causes.first_wrong_stage: merge (stem-conflict resolver + generic overwrite) and contamination-guard false positive
root_causes.fix: 1) _stem_reject_reason now only flags token-containment for DECLARATIVE or >250-char text (a question-shaped short stem restated by its solution is kept); 2) merge never lets a contaminated incoming stem replace a valid one (stem-conflict + generic write guards); 3) targeted_retry switches to a STEM-REGION-ONLY prompt after one contamination block; 4) Q-pass no longer runs on pure-solution windows (upstream contamination source), with 1-page cross-section overlap at the Q/S boundary preserving boundary-spanning question tails.

root_causes.title: Answer-missing records' rescue targets the wrong page (question page, not the key page) and key pages without the 'Answer Key' header are missed
evidence: ch15 q15 missing answer; [RESCUE] page 194: q15 -> 0 field(s) filled (194 is a question page; the key row is elsewhere)
ch7 4 missing answers; rescue pages 100/105 -> 0 filled
ch2 q25 missing answer + bad options + missing stem (the q_no=None option-definition fragments were never reconciled)
root_causes.mechanism: locate_missing_record_pages only matched answer rows on pages carrying the KEY_TABLE_PROBE header, and only in '| qn |' pipe format; a key page with '13. B' rows and no header was never located, so the answer-only rescue asked the wrong page and the record shipped answer=null.
root_causes.fix: answer-row matchers now run on EVERY page in pipe ('| 13 | B |'), list ('13. B') and dash ('13 - B') formats, header optional; header pages still get a stronger vote. The answer-only rescue prompt targets the located key page.

root_causes.title: MAX_CALLS_PER_DAY=1400 never fired; the run hit the model's REAL 500 RPD cap mid-chapter and wasted 2 calls on the 429 backoff before exiting
evidence: status=429 ... limit: 500, model: gemini-3.1-flash-lite ... [QUOTA] still limited after backoff -- saving, exiting
root_causes.mechanism: the self-brake was set for a 1500/day plan, but the free tier for this model is 500/day; the pipeline only stopped when the API rejected, burning 2 quota calls on the 65s backoff.
root_causes.fix: MAX_CALLS_PER_DAY=480 (graceful daily stop with ~20-call headroom; resume via state.json).

root_causes.title: Malformed-JSON A-pass falsely marked UNRESOLVED even when the same-batch re-ask fully recovered
evidence: [WARN] malformed JSON on A-pass pages [175..179] -- one same-batch re-ask
also malformed JSON A-pass 79-88 (10-page salvage recovered) and 503 on ch11 135-139 (single-page retry recovered)
root_causes.mechanism: pass_recovered was only set in the salvage-fail branch; a SUCCESSFUL same-batch re-ask left it False, so _classify_pass_status(had_error=True, recovered=False) -> UNRESOLVED even though the data came back.
root_causes.fix: pass_recovered = True after a successful same-batch re-ask; recovered passes are RETRYABLE_FAILURE, not UNRESOLVED.
